name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic win near-certain
Chris Rabb has strong fundraising and outside support; independent opponent raised only ~$11k
Prediction markets price the Democratic side around 97%
Open seat after Dwight Evans' retirement, but the seat stays with the party's strong lean
model.rationale: The D+40 district fundamentals dominate this open seat, and Rabb's roughly $1.3 million raised plus $1.6 million in outside support dwarfs Dennis Mahoney's token independent campaign. Markets price the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with a Safe D call.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded late outside campaign against Rabb could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
This Philadelphia-area House seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of about D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Chris Rabb enters the general election with a decisive resource advantage: roughly $1.3 million raised and over $1.5 million in outside support backing him. His opponent, independent Dennis Mahoney, has raised only about $11,000 with no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's overwhelming lean and the lopsided money picture, both pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
